concepts.title: Canvas Area of a Cylindrical-Conical Tent
concepts.definition: A tent made of a cylinder topped by a cone needs canvas equal to the curved surface of both parts: pi times radius times slant height for the cone, plus 2 pi times radius times height for the cylinder.
concepts.key_idea: Splitting the tent bill into small functions such as cyl(h,r) and con(l,r) keeps each area formula in one reusable place.
question_patterns: Compute the canvas area of a tent with cylinder height 5 m, radius 2 m and conical slant height 3 m.
Why is the curved surface formula of the cone different from that of the cylinder?
Rewrite the tent program using two user defined functions cyl and con and state what each returns.
A tent has radius 7 m, cylinder height 10 m and slant height 5 m. Find the total canvas used.
Which parts of the tent program change if the conical top is replaced by a taller cone of the same radius?

solution_steps.explain: Curved surface of a cone is pi times radius times slant height.
Curved surface of a cylinder is 2 pi times radius times height.
The canvas covers both parts.

worked_examples.q: Using pi = 3.14, what is the curved area of a cylindrical canvas wall of radius 3 m and height 5 m?

concepts.title: Post-Tax Net Price Function
concepts.definition: The payable amount for the tent adds 18 percent tax to the canvas cost; wrapping this in a function post_tax_price(cost) lets any product reuse the same tax step.
concepts.key_idea: A tax of 18 percent multiplies the cost by 0.18, and the customer pays cost plus that tax.
question_patterns: A canvas costing 28574 rupees attracts 18 percent tax. What is the net amount payable?
Write the function post_tax_price that returns the payable amount for a given cost.
Why is the post_tax_price function reusable for products other than tents?
The net payable for a tent is 11800 rupees including 18 percent tax. Estimate the pre-tax cost.
What value does post_tax_price return when the cost argument is 1000?

solution_steps.explain: 18 percent of the cost is 0.18 times it.
The net price is cost plus tax.

worked_examples.q: A canvas costs Rs 2000 before tax. With 18 percent tax added, what is the payable amount in rupees?

concepts.title: The pow Function with a Modulus Argument
concepts.definition: The built-in pow(x, y) raises x to the power y, and a third argument makes it return the remainder of that power on division by the modulus; other built-ins such as abs, max, min, sum and len inspect or aggregate values.
concepts.formula: pow(x, y, z) = x ** y % z
concepts.key_idea: pow(5, 2, 4) first squares 5 to get 25, then keeps only the remainder on division by 4.
concepts.textbook_ref: kecs107.txt, Table 7.1 rows pow and sum
question_patterns: What does pow(5, 2, 4) return, and in what order are the two operations applied?
Differentiate the built-in pow() from math.pow() with one example.
Evaluate divmod(7, 2) and name the two parts of its result.
What does sum([2, 4, 7, 3], 3) return, and why?
Which built-in counts the elements of a list, and what does len('Patience') give?
Compute abs(-5.7) and max(23, 4, 56).

solution_steps.action: raise the base to the exponent
solution_steps.explain: The power is formed first.
The remainder on division by z is the final result.

worked_examples.q: What does pow(5, 2, 4) return in Python?

concepts.title: Mean of Floating Values in a List
concepts.definition: A user defined function can walk a list with a for loop, folding every element into a running total while counting the elements, and the mean is the total divided by that count.
concepts.key_idea: The loop does two jobs at once: accumulating the sum and counting how many values entered it.
question_patterns: For the list [1.3, 2.4, 3.5, 6.9], what mean does myMean print?
Write a function myMean(myList) that computes the mean of the values stored in a list.
Why must the counter be incremented inside the same loop that adds the elements?
Four readings 2.0, 3.5, 4.0 and 6.5 are averaged. What mean results?
What happens to the mean if the counter is left at zero?

solution_steps.explain: Each pass adds one element into the total.
Four elements entered the list, so divide by 4.

worked_examples.q: Four values sum to 88. What is their mean?

concepts.title: Mixed Fraction from an Improper Fraction
concepts.definition: The function mixedFraction(num, deno = 1) converts an improper fraction into a whole part plus a proper remainder: floor division gives the whole part, the modulus gives the leftover numerator, and deno falls back to its default value 1 when no argument is supplied.
concepts.key_idea: A default parameter must trail in the header, so def mixedFraction(num, deno = 1) is legal but placing the default first is not.
concepts.textbook_ref: kecs107.txt, Program 7-9 and the default-parameter note
question_patterns: Convert the improper fraction 17 / 2 into a mixed fraction the way mixedFraction does.
What does mixedFraction(9) print, and why does deno become 1?
Why is def calcInterest(principal = 1000, rate, time = 5) rejected as a header?
A fraction 22 / 5 is passed to the function. Give the whole part and the remainder shown.
When does mixedFraction report that the fraction evaluates to a whole number?

solution_steps.explain: Floor division counts how many times deno fits into num.
The modulus keeps what cannot form another whole unit.
Whole part plus the fractional share gives the mixed value.

worked_examples.q: In mixedFraction(22, 5), what whole part does floor division give?

concepts.title: Compound Interest via a User Defined Function
concepts.definition: Compound interest grows the principal by the factor (1 + r/n) raised to n times t, where r is the yearly rate, n the compounding count per year and t the years; the interest is the grown amount minus the principal.
concepts.formula: interest = principal * (1 + rate / periods) ** (periods * years) - principal
concepts.key_idea: Compounding more often per year multiplies the growth factor more times, so the interest rises.
question_patterns: Compute the compound interest on 5000 rupees at 8 percent compounded quarterly for 2 years.
Write a function that accepts principal, rate, time and the number of compounding periods, and returns the compound interest.
Why does the exponent use periods times years rather than just years?
Which earns more after 2 years on the same principal: 8 percent yearly or 8 percent half-yearly? Justify.
State the growth factor applied in each compounding period when the yearly rate is 10 percent and compounding is monthly.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the yearly rate across the periods and add 1.

solution_steps.action: raise it to the period count
solution_steps.explain: The factor compounds once per period over all years.
Multiply the principal by the compounded factor.
Interest is the gain over the original sum.

worked_examples.q: Rs 1000 grows at 10 percent per year compounded yearly. What is the amount after 2 years, in rupees?

concepts.title: Determinant of a Quadratic Expression
concepts.definition: For a quadratic with coefficients a, b and c, the determinant b squared minus 4ac decides the nature of roots: positive signals two real roots, zero a repeated root, and negative no real root.
concepts.key_idea: The sign test on the determinant is the condition the function checks before reporting its verdict.
question_patterns: Calculate the determinant for a = 1, b = 5, c = 6 and state the nature of the roots.
Write a function that accepts three coefficients and returns the value b squared minus 4ac.
What root nature does a determinant of exactly zero indicate?
For a = 2, b = 4, c = 5, evaluate the determinant and report the result.
Which condition should the function test to print that real roots do not exist?

solution_steps.explain: The term b squared comes first.
Multiply the outer coefficients and scale by 4.
Determinant equals b squared minus 4ac.

worked_examples.q: For a = 1, b = 5 and c = 6, what is the determinant b^2 - 4ac?

concepts.title: Global and Local Scope of Variables
concepts.definition: A variable created outside every function is global and reachable anywhere, while one created inside a function is local and vanishes when the function ends; assigning to a global name inside a function without the global keyword would silently create a local twin instead.
concepts.formula: scope = global (outside all functions) or local (inside one)
concepts.key_idea: Printing a local variable after its function has ended raises NameError, as Program 7-14 shows.
question_patterns: Why does accessing the variable y after myFunc1 ends raise a NameError?
Differentiate a global variable from a local variable with one example of each.
What does prefixing the global keyword to num inside a function change about assignment?
A function defines local_variable = 5 while a global of the same name exists. Which one does the function see?
How long does a local variable survive in memory?
In Program 7-15, why does the printed num outside the function show 10 rather than 5?

solution_steps.explain: Assignments at module level create globals usable everywhere; assignments inside a function create locals that disappear at return unless declared global.

worked_examples.q: A variable created outside every function has what scope?

worked_examples.title: Full bill for a tent
worked_examples.problem: A tent has cylinder height 5 m, radius 2 m and conical slant height 3 m. Canvas costs 350 rupees per square metre. Find the canvas area, the cost, and the net payable after 18 percent tax.

steps.explain: Multiply area by the unit price.

worked_examples.answer_note: The canvas measures 81.64 square metres, costing 28574 rupees, and the customer pays 33717.32 rupees with tax.

worked_examples.title: Quarterly compound interest on savings
worked_examples.problem: A deposit of 5000 rupees earns 8 percent per annum compounded quarterly for 2 years. Compute the compound interest.

steps.explain: 8 percent split over 4 quarters is 2 percent per period.
Raise the growth factor to the period count.
Apply the factor, then remove the principal.

worked_examples.answer_note: The factor is about 1.171659, so the interest is about 858.30 rupees.
